title: The humble tea bag
paragraphs: Are you a tea drinker? If so, you’re not alone. Every day around the world millions of cups of this popular brew are drunk, and it’s been that way for thousands of years. The oldest discovered tea is from the Han Dynasty, dating from 206BC to 220AD. But it’s thought that the tea trend really took off during the Tang Dynasty in the 8th Century, when it became China’s national drink. Now, Turkey, the Republic of Ireland and the UK are believed to be the biggest tea-drinking nations, per capita.

Tea is consumed in many ways – slurped, sipped or glugged. It can be poured from pots, infused or brewed in the cup using tea bags – and it’s this latter process that is causing concern. Research last year found some premium tea bags might be leaving billions of microscopic plastic particles in the cup. Scientists from McGill University in Montreal found that some ‘plastic’ tea bags shed high levels of microplastics into water. However, The World Health Organization says such particles in drinking water do not appear to pose a risk.

Most tea bags are made from paper, with a small amount of plastic used to seal them shut – made from oil. This has led to debate about whether they can be recycled, but many are still composted. However, gardener Mike Armitage has told the BBC that the plastic contained in the soil could be washed into streams and rivers and ultimately out to sea.

Unilever, the owners of the tea brand PG Tips, said their tea bags are made with a small amount of plastic – used to seal them – and that they are suitable for composting. And the brand Yorkshire Tea said their bags do contain 25% polypropylene, but they were “actively developing plant-based and biodegradable alternatives”.

While tea bag manufacturers might be doing their bit to reduce plastic pollution, it could be a good time to switch your favourite beverage to coffee, or if that isn’t your cup of tea then try using loose-leaf tea, which can have a better flavour.

vocabulary.example: This brew is a blend of different types of tea.
vocabulary.translation: 这种饮品是由多种茶叶混合制成的。

vocabulary.example: The tradition dates from the Ming Dynasty.
vocabulary.translation: 这个传统可以追溯到明朝。

vocabulary.entry: take off /teɪk ɒf/ （潮流、事业等）兴起；腾飞
vocabulary.example: The new fashion trend took off quickly among young people.
vocabulary.translation: 这种新的时尚潮流很快在年轻人中流行起来。

vocabulary.example: The country has a high income per capita.
vocabulary.translation: 这个国家的人均收入很高。

vocabulary.entry: slurp /slɜːp/ v. 出声地喝；大口啜饮
vocabulary.example: He slurped his soup noisily.
vocabulary.translation: 他大声地喝汤。

vocabulary.example: She sipped the hot tea slowly to avoid burning her tongue.
vocabulary.translation: 她慢慢小口抿着热茶，以免烫到舌头。

vocabulary.example: He glugged the juice down in seconds.
vocabulary.translation: 他几秒钟就把果汁大口喝完了。

vocabulary.example: Allow the herbs to infuse in hot water for ten minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 把草药放在热水中冲泡十分钟。

vocabulary.example: Of the two options, I prefer the latter one.
vocabulary.translation: 在这两个选项中，我更喜欢后者。

vocabulary.entry: premium /ˈpriːmiəm/ adj. 高端的；优质的
vocabulary.example: The shop sells premium coffee beans imported from Brazil.
vocabulary.translation: 这家商店售卖从巴西进口的优质咖啡豆。

vocabulary.entry: microscopic /ˌmaɪkrəˈskɒpɪk/ adj. 微小的；微观的
vocabulary.example: The microscope can show us microscopic organisms.
vocabulary.translation: 显微镜能让我们看到微生物。

vocabulary.entry: plastic particle /ˈplæstɪk ˈpɑːtɪkl/ n. 塑料颗粒
vocabulary.example: The beach was covered with tiny plastic particles.
vocabulary.translation: 沙滩上布满了细小的塑料颗粒。

vocabulary.example: The tree sheds its leaves every autumn.
vocabulary.translation: 这棵树每年秋天都会落叶。

vocabulary.example: Microplastics have been found in various marine creatures.
vocabulary.translation: 在多种海洋生物体内都发现了微塑料。

vocabulary.entry: pose a risk /pəʊz ə rɪsk/ 构成威胁
vocabulary.example: Smoking poses a serious risk to your health.
vocabulary.translation: 吸烟会对你的健康构成严重威胁。

vocabulary.example: Please seal the envelope before posting it.
vocabulary.translation: 邮寄前请把信封封好。

vocabulary.example: We should recycle glass and paper to protect the environment.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该回收玻璃和纸张来保护环境。

vocabulary.example: We can compost vegetable peelings in the garden.
vocabulary.translation: 我们可以在花园里把蔬菜皮制成堆肥。

vocabulary.example: Polypropylene is widely used in making plastic containers.
vocabulary.translation: 聚丙烯被广泛用于制造塑料容器。

vocabulary.entry: biodegradable /ˌbaɪəʊdɪˈɡreɪdəbl/ adj. 可生物降解的
vocabulary.example: These bags are made of biodegradable material.
vocabulary.translation: 这些袋子是由可生物降解材料制成的。

vocabulary.example: The restaurant offers a variety of hot and cold beverages.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅提供多种冷热饮品。

vocabulary.entry: loose-leaf tea /ˌluːs liːf ˈtiː/ n. 散装茶叶
vocabulary.example: Loose-leaf tea usually has a richer flavour than tea bags.
vocabulary.translation: 散装茶叶通常比茶包的味道更浓郁。

sentences.english: The oldest discovered tea is from the Han Dynasty, dating from 206BC to 220AD.
sentences.chinese: 目前发现的最古老的茶叶来自公元前206年至公元220年的汉朝。

sentences.english: Now, Turkey, the Republic of Ireland and the UK are believed to be the biggest tea-drinking nations, per capita.
sentences.chinese: 如今，土耳其、爱尔兰共和国和英国被认为是全球人均饮茶量最高的国家。

sentences.english: Tea is consumed in many ways – slurped, sipped or glugged.
sentences.chinese: 茶的饮用方式多种多样——可大口啜饮、小口抿饮，也可豪饮。

sentences.english: It can be poured from pots, infused or brewed in the cup using tea bags – and it’s this latter process that is causing concern.
sentences.chinese: 茶可以从茶壶中倒出饮用，也可以用茶包在杯中冲泡——而正是这后一种冲泡方式引发了人们的担忧。

sentences.english: Research last year found some premium tea bags might be leaving billions of microscopic plastic particles in the cup.
sentences.chinese: 去年的一项研究发现，一些高端茶包可能会在杯中留下数十亿个微小的塑料颗粒。

sentences.english: Scientists from McGill University in Montreal found that some ‘plastic’ tea bags shed high levels of microplastics into water.
sentences.chinese: 蒙特利尔麦吉尔大学的科学家们发现，一些“塑料材质”的茶包会向水中释放大量微塑料。

sentences.english: However, The World Health Organization says such particles in drinking water do not appear to pose a risk.
sentences.chinese: 不过，世界卫生组织表示，饮用水中的这类塑料颗粒似乎并不会构成健康威胁。

sentences.english: Most tea bags are made from paper, with a small amount of plastic used to seal them shut – made from oil.
sentences.chinese: 大多数茶包的材质是纸，会使用少量以石油为原料制成的塑料来封口。

sentences.english: This has led to debate about whether they can be recycled, but many are still composted.
sentences.chinese: 这引发了关于茶包能否回收利用的争论，但许多茶包仍会被用于堆肥。

sentences.english: However, gardener Mike Armitage has told the BBC that the plastic contained in the soil could be washed into streams and rivers and ultimately out to sea.
sentences.chinese: 不过，园丁迈克·阿米蒂奇向英国广播公司表示，混入土壤中的塑料可能会被冲刷到小溪和河流中，最终流入大海。

sentences.english: Unilever, the owners of the tea brand PG Tips, said their tea bags are made with a small amount of plastic – used to seal them – and that they are suitable for composting.
sentences.chinese: 联合利华集团是茶饮品牌PG Tips的母公司，该集团表示，旗下茶包仅使用少量塑料用于封口，且这些茶包适合堆肥处理。

sentences.english: And the brand Yorkshire Tea said their bags do contain 25% polypropylene, but they were “actively developing plant-based and biodegradable alternatives”.
sentences.chinese: 约克郡茶品牌则称，其茶包确实含有25%的聚丙烯成分，但该品牌“正在积极研发植物基且可生物降解的替代品”。

sentences.english: While tea bag manufacturers might be doing their bit to reduce plastic pollution, it could be a good time to switch your favourite beverage to coffee, or if that isn’t your cup of tea then try using loose-leaf tea, which can have a better flavour.
sentences.chinese: 尽管茶包制造商们在为减少塑料污染尽自己的一份力，但或许现在是时候把你最爱的饮品换成咖啡了；如果你对咖啡不感兴趣，那么不妨试试散装茶叶，它的口感会更好。
